thesis: This episode argues that during the dot-com bubble, market valuations for technology companies were detached from fundamental reality, often trading at extreme multiples of earnings or revenue despite low sales or losses. The speaker contrasts these inflated tech stocks with traditional industrial and financial companies, which appeared more reasonably priced relative to their earnings. Ultimately, the thesis suggests that the market was pricing in a future that did not exist, creating a dangerous disconnect between stock prices and actual business performance.
